text.p: September T-bond futures look more positive on Thursday and are set for a move towards 113-30, 31, technical analysts said.
Sam Malone-Jansens, analyst on the futures desk at Lloyds Bank in London said the bullish sentiment was suggested by a number of technical factors.
"Two key points yesterday were that we had both an outside day and a bullish engulfing pattern on Japanese candlesticks," he said.
Added to this, a 3-1/2 month rising support line was still intact, he said.
"It was violated on an intra-day basis on August 13 but not on a closing basis, so that's not significant. The key thing is we are still holding on to it," he added.
Malone-Jansens said a move higher was also suggested by nine-day slow Stochastics which had broken out of oversold territory.
"So the pattern is set for some structured gains," he said.
At 1100 GMT, September T-bond futures were at 113-05, up 10 ticks from Wednesday's Chicago settlement.
To the upside, Malone-Jansens said initial resistance was offered from Wednesday's isolated high at 113-19.
Above there, a 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the decline from 116-31 came in at 113-28, just before a good congestion level at 113-30 to 113-31.
"That is the near term target," he said.
To the downside, the current level on the 3-1/2 month rising trendline would offer support at 112-17.
"Below that there is a tight secondary level of congestion at 112-14 and then natural support between 112-01 and 111-31," Malone-Jansens said.
But some analysts said the picture for T-bonds was less certain.
Technical analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London said according to Elliott waves Wednesday's low could have been wave five "putting US bonds in a second wave rally."
Alternatively they said the contract had been in an irregular b-wave of the fourth wave at 111-31, and had completed that fourth wave at 113-19 so had now entered the fifth wave.
"Bonds must then resume the drop today and at least get below 112-04," the DMG analysts said in a research note. "A move to 110-23/111-15 remains preferred."
Only on a rise above 113-19 would this view be negated, they said.
At the short end, December Eurodollar futures were at 94.075, up 0.015 on the day.
